phone-number-value.q1: How is a phone number valued?
phone-number-value.a1: By the patterns buyers pay for: the same digit repeated at the end (888, 8888), a straight such as 12345, pairs like AABB or ABAB, lucky endings, and few different digits. The strongest pattern sets the price band and the rest place the number inside it.
phone-number-value.q2: Is this the price I can sell my number for?
phone-number-value.a2: No. It is a rule-based estimate of how sought after the number is. Real prices depend on the carrier, any plan tied to the number, whether the number can be transferred, and the buyer.
phone-number-value.a3: In Chinese and Vietnamese, 8 sounds like getting rich, 6 like things going smoothly and 9 like a long time. The number 4 sounds like "death" in Chinese, so patterns built on 4 sell for less there.
phone-number-value.a4: A folk method popular in China: take the last four digits, divide by 80 and keep the remainder (0 counts as 80). The number from 1 to 80 is looked up in a traditional table of lucky and unlucky numbers. It is for fun.
phone-number-value.a5: No. The number is read and valued in your browser and never leaves the page.

license-plate-value.q1: How much is my private number plate worth?
license-plate-value.a1: In the UK, shorter marks are worth more: dateless marks such as "1 A" or "ABC 1" are the dearest, then prefix and suffix marks, then current-style marks. The estimate follows those bands and adds for a single 1 or repeated letters or digits.
license-plate-value.q2: Why does a Vietnamese plate with 88888 cost so much?
license-plate-value.a2: Vietnam sells plates at public auction. Five of a kind (ngũ quý) such as 51K-888.88 has sold for tens of billions of dong; four of a kind, straights such as 123.45 and three of a kind follow.
license-plate-value.q3: Can I sell a Chinese licence plate?
license-plate-value.a3: No. In mainland China plates are issued, not sold, so the figure for a Chinese plate only shows how good the number is, not a price you can get.
license-plate-value.q4: Does a plate that spells a name cost more?
license-plate-value.a4: Often much more, but this tool cannot tell which letters a buyer wants. Treat the estimate as the floor for name and word plates.
license-plate-value.a5: No. The plate is read and valued in your browser.

domain-value.q1: How is a domain name valued?
domain-value.a1: By the extension (.com first), the length, whether the name is a common word or two words, a short number or acronym, and whether it is easy to say. Hyphens, digits mixed with letters and long names lower the value.
domain-value.a2: It is a rule-based estimate from the name alone. Traffic, existing sites, trademarks and one keen buyer can move a real price far from it. Compare with recent sales of similar names before you buy or sell.
domain-value.q3: Why is .com worth more than other extensions?
domain-value.a3: Most people type .com by habit, and most businesses want it. The same name under .ai, .io or .net usually sells for a fraction of the .com price.
domain-value.a4: Names made only of digits, such as 8888.com. Short ones sell well, especially to Chinese buyers; 8, 6 and 9 add value and 4 takes it away.
domain-value.q5: Does the tool look up the domain?
domain-value.a5: No. Nothing is sent anywhere; the name is valued in your browser, so it does not check whether the domain is registered.

car-depreciation.q1: How much does a car depreciate per year?
car-depreciation.a1: A common rule of thumb is about 20% in the first year and about 15% a year for the next four, so a car keeps about 40% of its price after five years. After that the loss slows to about 10% a year.
car-depreciation.a2: Luxury cars and electric cars usually lose value faster than average; pickups and many SUVs hold value better. Pick the type that fits your car.
car-depreciation.q3: How do miles or kilometres change the value?
car-depreciation.a3: The calculator assumes about 12,000 miles (19,300 km) a year. Each 10% more takes about 2% off the value, each 10% less adds about 2%, up to 20% either way.
car-depreciation.q4: Is this my car's trade-in value?
car-depreciation.a4: No. It is an estimate from typical depreciation. Model, local demand, service history and accidents matter; check local listings or a dealer quote for a price.
car-depreciation.a5: Any. Type the price in your currency and the results are in the same currency.

net-worth.q1: How do I calculate my net worth?
net-worth.a1: Add up everything you own (cash, investments, retirement savings, the value of your home and cars) and subtract everything you owe (mortgage, car loans, student loans, credit cards). The result is your net worth.
net-worth.q2: What is a good net worth for my age?
net-worth.a2: Enter your age to compare with the median and mean household net worth for that age group in the U.S. Federal Reserve's 2022 Survey of Consumer Finances. The median is the middle household; the mean is pulled up by the richest.
net-worth.a3: Yes, at what it would sell for today, and put the mortgage under debts. Count cars at their resale value, not what you paid.
net-worth.a4: Yes, when debts are larger than assets, which is common early in a career with student loans.
net-worth.q5: Are my numbers saved or sent?
net-worth.a5: No. Everything is worked out in your browser and nothing is stored.

business-valuation.q1: How do you value a small business?
business-valuation.a1: Most small businesses are priced at a multiple of yearly profit (seller's discretionary earnings, or EBITDA for larger firms). A revenue multiple and a discounted cash flow are useful checks.
business-valuation.a2: Pick an industry for a typical range: owner-run service, retail and restaurant businesses often sell for about 1.5–3.5 times profit, while software businesses fetch much more. Edit the multiples if you know better ones for your market.
business-valuation.a3: A discounted cash flow adds up the cash the business should make in future years, each worth less the further away it is, plus a terminal value for the years after the forecast.
business-valuation.q4: What discount rate should I use?
business-valuation.a4: Small private businesses are risky, so buyers often use 15–25%. A larger, steady company might use 8–12%. The rate must be above the terminal growth rate.
business-valuation.a5: No. It is an estimate for planning. A sale, loan or tax matter needs a qualified valuer.
